(2026)", "metaDescription": "Kodely generates real React code from a chat prompt and pay-per-build credits. Squarespace gives you polished templates, e-commerce, and a subscription. Here is the honest breakdown.", "targetKeyword": "kodely vs squarespace", "category": "Comparisons", "bodyHtml": "

Squarespace has spent over a decade perfecting the all-in-one hosted website: pick a template, drag some blocks, launch. Kodely takes a different route entirely — you describe the site in chat and it writes a real Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 app behind the scenes. Both get you a live site. How you get there, what you end up owning, and what you pay for are almost nothing alike.

This comparison is not going to pretend Kodely already beats Squarespace at everything — it does not. Here is where each one actually wins.

TL;DR verdict

FactorKodelySquarespace
How you buildDescribe the site in a chat interface; AI generates real componentsChoose a template, edit visually block by block
OutputReal .tsx source files you can view and copy in-appProprietary, closed system — no exportable code
PricingPay-per-build credits; 750 free on signup, no card requiredRecurring monthly or annual subscription
DomainFree <name>.kodely.site subdomain (no custom domains yet)Custom domain included
Template libraryNone — every site is generated from scratch via chatLarge library of designer-made templates
E-commerce / bookingNot available yetBuilt-in store and Acuity-powered booking
Editing modelChat-based edits, with free checkpoints to roll backVisual, click-to-edit builder

Pricing and the credit model

Squarespace runs on a recurring subscription — you pay every month or every year whether you touch the site or not. Kodely runs on credits that meter actual AI cost: 750 credits free at signup with no credit card, then top-ups at $9 for 500 credits, $40 for 2,500 credits (the most popular option), or $90 for 6,000 credits. Credits never expire, and a generation that fails to compile is never charged. If you want to build once, publish, and barely touch it again, Kodely's model means you are not paying a subscription for a site that is not changing. If you need ongoing store transactions, bookings, and a platform that handles everything indefinitely, a subscription like Squarespace's is the more predictable fit.

Do you actually own the code?

This is the sharpest difference between the two. Squarespace's output is entirely proprietary — there is no exportable code, no way to take your site and run it somewhere else. You are building inside their platform, permanently. Kodely generates a real, readable React and TypeScript codebase, and you can view and copy every generated file directly in-app. That said, be precise about what Kodely offers today: there is no zip export or download yet, so you are copying files by hand rather than pulling a full project archive. It is a meaningfully more open system than Squarespace's closed one, just not a finished one-click export experience.

Hosting and going live

Squarespace hosting is bundled with the subscription and includes a custom domain from day one — you can point a real domain like yourbusiness.com at it immediately. Kodely's one-click Publish puts your site live on a free <name>.kodely.site subdomain instantly, with every publish scanned for accidentally leaked secrets or API keys first. What Kodely does not have yet is custom domain support — if you need your own domain live today, Squarespace is the one that delivers that out of the box.

Design and template quality

Squarespace's biggest strength is its template library — genuinely designer-quality layouts built for portfolios, creative studios, and small businesses, with a curated visual editor that keeps things tighter than more sprawling builders like Wix. Kodely has no template library at all; there is nothing to browse and nothing to pick. Every site starts from a chat description and gets built component by component. That is faster if you know exactly what you want and would rather describe it than search through themes, but if you want a proven, polished visual starting point, Squarespace's templates are still the stronger design foundation.

E-commerce and booking depth

Squarespace has real depth here: a built-in store with inventory, checkout, and payments, plus Acuity-powered appointment booking baked into the platform. Kodely does not generate backends, databases, payments, or booking systems today — it is a front-end app builder, not a commerce platform. If selling products or taking bookings online is core to your site, Squarespace is currently the only one of the two that actually handles it.

Security

Every Kodely publish is automatically scanned for leaked secrets and API keys before it goes live, which matters because AI-generated code can otherwise expose credentials without anyone noticing. Squarespace's security posture is the standard hosted-platform model — you are trusting their infrastructure and do not manage anything yourself, which is simple but gives you no visibility into what is actually running.

Best for

Pick Squarespace if you want a polished, designer-grade template, built-in e-commerce or booking, and a custom domain live today, and you are fine with a closed system and a recurring subscription. Pick Kodely if you want to describe a site in plain English and get a real, inspectable React codebase back, you are comfortable on a free .kodely.site subdomain for now, and you would rather pay per build than commit to a monthly plan.

FAQ

Can I move a Kodely site to my own domain? Not yet — Kodely currently publishes only to free <name>.kodely.site subdomains.

Can I export my Squarespace site as code? No — Squarespace's output is fully proprietary with no code export.

Does Kodely have a template gallery like Squarespace? No. Kodely has no templates; every site is generated from your chat description.

Does Kodely support online stores? Not currently. Kodely does not generate backends, payments, or e-commerce functionality.

Is Kodely free to try? Yes — you get 750 credits on signup with no credit card required.

Ready to see what a chat prompt turns into? Start building free on Kodely.

This is the sharpest difference between the two. Squarespace's output is entirely proprietary — there is no exportable code, no way to take your site and run it somewhere else. Squarespace hosting is bundled with the subscription and includes a custom domain from day one — you can point a real domain like yourbusiness.com at it immediately. Squarespace's biggest strength is its template library — genuinely designer-quality layouts built for portfolios, creative studios, and small businesses, with a curated visual editor that keeps things tighter than more sprawling builders like Wix. Squarespace has real depth here: a built-in store with inventory, checkout, and payments, plus Acuity-powered appointment booking baked into the platform. Every Kodely publish is automatically scanned for leaked secrets and API keys before it goes live, which matters because AI-generated code can otherwise expose credentials without anyone noticing. Squarespace's security posture is the standard hosted-platform model — you are trusting their infrastructure and do not manage anything yourself, which is simple but gives you no visibility into what is actually running.
